title: Space to Ground: Splashdown in the Atlantic: Sept. 8, 2023
description: NASA's Space to Ground is your weekly update on what's happening aboard the International Space Station.
keywords: S2G 489, International Space Station, SpaceX Crew 6, Soyuz
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: WELCOME TO SPACE TO GROUND. I'M KAYLA LAFRANCE
THIS WEEK STARTED OUT WITH A SPLASH AS ONE DRAGON MISSION COMES TO A CLOSE.
ON SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 3RD, THE MEMBERS OF NASA’S SPACEX CREW-6,
NASA ASTRONAUTS STEPHEN BOWEN AND WOODY HOBURG,
UAE ASTRONAUT SULTAN ALNEYADI, AND ROSCOSMOS COSMONAUT ANDREY FEDYAEV
UNDOCKED FROM THE SPACE STATION.
SEVERAL HOURS LATER, THE CREW-DRAGON ENDEAVOUR
REENTERED THE EARTH’S ASTMOSPHERE AND BEGAN ITS DECENT.
FOUR MINUTES BEFORE SPLASHDOWN, THE DRAGON WAS TRAVELING
AT 350 MPH AND WAS AT AN ALTITUDE OF 18000 FEET
WHEN THE DROGUE PARACHUTES DEPLOYED.
AND LESS THAN A MINUTE LATER, THE MAIN PARACHUTES DEPLOYED
AT ABOUT 6,000 FEET ALTITUDE WHILE THE SPACECRAFT
HAD SLOWED TO 120 MILES PER HOUR.
ENDEAVOUR LANDED SAFELY IN THE EARLY MORNING HOURS
OF SEPTEMBER 4TH OFF THE COAST OF JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA,
AFTER 186 DAYS IN SPACE.
TEAMS ON THE SPACEX RECOVERY SHIP SECURED THE DRAGON
AND HOIST THE CAPSULE ONTO THE MAIN DECK
WITH THE ASTRONAUTS INSIDE.
ONCE ON THE MAIN DECK, THE CREW WAS TAKEN OUT OF THE SPACECRAFT
AND RECEIVE MEDICAL CHECKS BEFORE A HELICOPTER RIDE
TO BOARD A PLANE FOR HOUSTON TO BE REUNITED WITH FRIENDS AND FAMILY.
THE NEXT SOYUZ MISSION TO THE SPACE STATION IS GETTING CLOSER
AND ITS CREW IS UNDERGOING THEIR FINAL TRAINING
AND CHECKS BEFORE THEY HEAD TO ORBIT.
THE MISSION WILL CARRY TWO RUSSIAN COSMONAUTS
AND NASA ASTRONAUT LORAL O’HARA INTO ORBIT FOR THEIR LONG DURATION FLIGHT.
CURRENTLY PLANNED FOR SEPTEMBER 15, 70S WILL LAUNCH ATOP A SOYUZ ROCKET
FROM THE BAIKONUR COSMODROME BEFORE RENDEZVOUSING
AND DOCKING LATER THAT DAY TO THE SPACE STATION.
LIVE COVERAGE WILL BE PROVIDED FOR ALL UPCOMING LAUNCH AND DOCKING EVENTS
SO FOLLOW US ON SOCIAL MEDIA, OR HEAD OVER TO NASA TELEVISION,
THE NASA APP, OR THE AGENCY’S WEBSITE FOR MORE INFORMATION AND TIMES
AND THAT’S SPACE TO GROUND FOR THIS WEEK.
THANKS FOR WATCHING.
